prompt: What is the name of H2Se(aq)?

choices.why: That is its name when it isn't dissolved in water. The (aq) label makes it an acid.
An acid of hydrogen and just one other element takes the hydro- prefix.
An acid of hydrogen and one other element always ends in -ic acid; -ous comes from anions ending in -ite.

explanation: H2Se(aq) is made of hydrogen and only one other element, so its name is hydro- + the stem of the element + -ic acid: hydroselenic acid.

prompt: HCl is written without an (aq) label. What is its name?

choices.why: That name is for HCl(aq), dissolved in water. Without the (aq) label, HCl is treated as a molecular compound.
Chloric acid is HClO3(aq), from the chlorate ion.

explanation: The (aq) label shows that a compound is dissolved in water. Without it, HCl is treated as a molecular compound, hydrogen chloride; dissolved in water, it is hydrochloric acid.

prompt: The chlorite ion is ClO2−. What is the name of HClO2(aq)?

choices.why: -ic acid comes from an anion ending in -ate: chlorate, ClO3−, gives chloric acid.
The hydro- prefix is only for acids of hydrogen and one other element. This acid contains a polyatomic ion.
The anion's ending changes: -ite becomes -ous acid.

explanation: An acid made from a polyatomic anion takes its name from the anion's stem. Chlorite ends in -ite, so the acid is chlor- + -ous acid: chlorous acid.

prompt: The carbonate ion is CO3^2−. What is the formula of carbonic acid?

choices.why: Carbonate has a 2− charge, so it takes two H+ ions to balance it.
The acid keeps the whole carbonate ion, CO3, so there are three oxygen atoms.

explanation: Carbonate ends in -ate, so its acid is carbonic acid. The acid is H+ ions with the carbonate ion, and CO3^2− needs two H+ to balance its charge: H2CO3(aq).

prompt: Which of these is a property of acids?

choices.text: Many react with some metals to form oxygen gas
choices.why: Acids that react with metals form metal ions and elemental hydrogen, not oxygen.

choices.text: They are rarely found in foods
choices.why: Acids are common in foods: citrus fruits, vinegar, spinach, and some soft drinks all contain them.

explanation: Acids taste sour (the sourness of citrus fruits and vinegar comes from acids), many react with some metals to form metal ions and hydrogen, and they change the colors of certain plant pigments.

prompt: Which acid is found in spinach and other green leafy vegetables?

choices.why: Citric acid is in citrus fruits.
Phosphoric acid is an ingredient in some soft drinks.
Hydrochloric acid is stomach acid, and it's also sold as a cleaner for concrete and masonry.

explanation: Oxalic acid, H2C2O4(aq), is found in spinach and other green leafy vegetables.
